answer.summary: Maggie recommends combining direct conversations with users and deliberate follow-up on results to learn why things happened—not relying on dashboards alone.

sections.heading: Talk directly with users
sections.content: She says most PMs will get more and better insight into why things are happening by talking to 10 users than by looking at any dashboard. The reason is that conversations reveal what users need and care about; she warns that emphasizing quantitative data can come at the expense of qualitative research and judgment. She allows that dashboards and experiments may work well in high-volume businesses where experiments are easy to run.

sections.heading: Follow up on what you ship
sections.content: She also recommends checking results after the initial launch period: set calendar reminders for two weeks, a month, and six months later to revisit the dashboard, metrics, or other relevant evidence, then share the results with people who care. She says following up helps PMs learn why something happened—or did not—and improve with each launch.
